andrew-jackson-andrew-fields-warrenton-1.A1:
POSSES HUNT NEGRO
WHO BREAKS PRISON
Pursuers Threaten Lynching Man Accused by Woman of Attacking Her.
WARRENTON, Va., Aug. 10.—Escaping from the jail here, where he has been held for an attack on the wife of a prominent resident, Andrew Jackson, alias Andrew Fields, is being hunted by a posse of more than 200 men, including some of the most prominent citizens of this section of the county.

Field was permitted to exercise in a room at the jail yesterday afternoon in the absence of Jailor J. W. Shirley, who was closing the court house. When the jailor returned to the cell room, he found Fields had escaped, climbing the high stone wall around the prison.

Within a half hour after the negro had escaped the man hunt started. Armed with rifles and revolvers, more than 200 residents set out on his trail.

Fields, was arrested three weeks ago, after he is said to have attacked Mrs. J. B. Wilson, who had raised him on her farm since he was a child. The trail led to Bealeton, where the negro formerly lived with the Wilson family. He was surrounded on the farm of Mrs. George Smith, but in the darkness eluded his pursuers in a field of tall corn.

Because of the alleged attack on Mrs. Wilson by Fields, it is feared that if he is captured, he will be lynched. Feeling is running high against Fields and open threats have been made. Three posses are searching for him in various parts of the county. It is believed he has reached the home of a negro in a colored settlement near here and that his capture is a matter of only a few hours.

It was learned Fields had passed over the farm of C. E. Tiffany, president of the Fauquier National Bank.

ASSERTS WARRENTON
LACKS MOB SPIRIT
Warrenton, Va., Aug. 14.—Little possibility exists of mob spirit breaking out in this city, asserts Mayor Austin O. Weedon, who points to the peaceable and orderly manner in which citizens assisted in the search for a colored jail breaker this week as evidence of his stand. Intense feeling and excitement was conspicuous by its absence during the day, Mayor Weedon declares. There was no threat of a mob or riot, he says. The negro, Andrew Jackson, charged with attempted assault on a white woman, is again lodged in the city jail.

Claude Chandler Found Early Today Hanging from from Tree Six Miles from from Capital; Taken from from Jail Last Night.
SHERIFF TOLD STORY BY PHONE; FINDS BODY
Body is Taken to Capital; Bullet Hole Through Head; Mob Worked in Harmony; Jail Officials Overpowered.
By United Press.

Oklahoma City, Aug. 30.—The body of Claude Chandler, the alleged slayer of the officers who raided his father's home near Arcadia Saturday morning, was found hanging to a tree six miles west of this city early today, according to the police.

Chandler was taken from the county jail Sunday night about 10 o'clock by a mob of armed and masked men who were admitted to the jail when one of the number posed as an officer and told Jailer J. B. Saunders that he had a prisoner he wished to place in place in the Oklahoma City jail for safe keeping over night.

The mob then worked with precision, cutting telephone wires and turning out lights while the negro was located and dragged from the jail to waiting automoibles in one of which he was spirited away.
Chandler was accused of killing Homer Adrean, deputy sheriff of Oklahoma county and Stanton Weiss, special prohibition officer, who with other officers raided the home of Chandler's father near Arcadia Saturday. A gun fight started while the raid was in progress, the elder Chandler being killed in addition to the two officers. Claude Chandler, the young negro was captured by officers' posse and was brought to Oklahoma City.

The story of the mob was given this morning to the sheriff by an unknown person who called up by phone. In the conversation the sheriff was told where the body of the negro could be found.

He hurried to the spot and dis covered the body hanging to a tree, entirely hidden by a clump of bushes. There was ab ullet hole in the head, it was discovered when the body was brought here.

Armed Negroes Are Reported En Route To Oklahoma City
Six motor cars containing armed negroes are reported to have left Edmonton, about 15 miles north of here, and three automobiles also ocntaining negroes are reported to have left Arcardia, about 23 miles northeast of here, for Oklahoma City, according to messages received at the office of County Attorney Cargill here shortly before noon. It was said at the county attorney's office that Cargill was arming his deputies in preparation for any eventuality.

A telephone message from the city marshal at Arcadia to authorities here said three cars containing 12 negroes had stopped there a short time and departed in the direction of Oklahoma City. The marshal said, however, he was unable to see any weapons and that they appeared to be in a friendly spirit.

Groups of negroes were gathered in the negro section of Oklahoma City at noon. About 200 men, all talking among themselves, were assembled only three blocks away from the business section, while scores of women and children sat on the front porches of their homes.

The body of Claude Chandler, negro, aged 19, who last night was taken from the jail here by a group of 30 masked men, early today was hanging from a tree near Council Grove, about eight miles west of Oklahoma City, according to a telephone message from a farmer to the sheriff's office here. Chandler was arrested Saturday in a raid upon an alleged moonshine still near Arcadia, Okla., in which Stanton Weiss, federal prohibition enforcement agent; Deputy Sheriff Homer Andrean and Charles Chandler, father of Claude handler, were killed.

TAKEN FROM OKLAHOMA COUNTY JAIL BY FRIENDS OF ADREAN AND WEISS
PROSECUTOR CARGILL PEREMPTORILY ORDERED 18-YEAR OLD BOY TO BE CONFINED IN OKLAHOMA COUNTY JAIL; NEGROES NEAR ARCADIA IN UGLY MOOD; MRS. CHANDLER'S STORY
A mob, alleged to have been made up principally of elective and appointive officers of Oklahoma county, and led by a deputy sheriff of Oklahoma county, took Claude Chandler from the Oklahoma county jail at 10 o'clock Sunday night and lynched him.

The mob was a "friendly" one. That is, it was friendly with the jailor, Saunders, and the inside men who pointed to the cell where Chandler was confined. About twenty-five men composed the party.

All were masked.

Sheriff Ed Robertson claims Deputy E. B. Moore led the bunch.

Chandler was placed in an automobile and driven to a point nine miles from Oklahoma City on the El Reno road.

The body contained a number of bullet holes.

It was not cut down until 9 o'clock this morning. It was taken to Meridian this afternoon for burial.

Every officer in Oklahoma county knew about the proposed lynching. "We must avenge Weics and Adrean," whispered the crowd.

Oklahoma City, Aug. 31.—Indications of a race uprising in Oklahoma and Logan counties reported to state and county officers here throughout the morning, yesterday, as the result of the lynching here Sunday night of Claude Chandler, negro, arrested for the killing of two officers who attempted to raid an alleged moonshine still 23 miles north of here early Saturday morning, had shown no developments late Monday afternoon and the opinion was expressed that no disorders were expected. Since the shooting of the officers Saturday morning, reports have been received here that negroes, congregating in large numbers in many towns and localities of the two counties were prepared to march on officials here, with revenge for the death of Chandler, as their motive. Bands of negroes grouped in many sections of Oklahoma City but no demonstrations have developed. Police were actively engaged in dispersing the negroes and were prepared to meet any emergency that might arise.

Reports from Arcadia and Edmond that armed negroes in motor cars were advancing on the city caused the county attorney's office here to arm three automobiles loaded with deputies and send them out to meet the negroes, but by a detour, both parties ailed to meet. Itw as afterwards learned that the greatest number of the negroes in the cars were relatives or friends of Chandler, and that their appaeent intention of visiting the city was to view the body of the dead negro. It was stated at the office of the county attorney that the negroes upon reaching here had no weapons and indicated no attitude of hostility toward officials or any of the enforcement officers.

Robertson on War-Path

Governor Robertson is wroth and says that the sheriffs of two counties should be removed from office. He addressed a stinging letter to the attorney general Monday afternoon, calling his attention to the act that mob violence was a disgrace to any state in which it was permitted, and that the law should be enforced and the members of the mobs brought to justice.

The Letter

The governor's letter follows:

"Through the daily press, I have learned of the recent lynchings at Tulsa, and Oklahoma City. These are the first that have occurred during this administration, and I hoped that no such act would ever disgrace the fair name of our state again.

Officers Have Not "Reported"

"I am unable at this time to give you the details because none of the officers of Tulsa or Oklahoma counties have seen fit to make any report whatsoever. They did not ask for aid, although I gather from the papers that in Tulsa there was widespread talk on the streets during the day to the effect that the lynching would be done. Also the same situation existed in Oklahoma City. Least, wise I have heard that talk this morning.

"The jail at Tulsa is on the third or fourth story of the courthouse and one determined man could have withstood a mob of several hundred people. LYNCHING GREATER THAN INVESTIGATING CRIME
However great may be the crime which causes lynching, the crime of lynching is greater than the crime which caused it, declares the Manufacturers' Record.

The criminal, vile as he may be, commits a crime against an individual, and in that way against society. But society, when through the mob it lynches a man, commits a greater crime, for it lynches the law and the sovereignty of the state. The mob crime is far greater in its effect for evil than is the crime for which the criminal was lynched. The mob spirit feeds on the lust of blood. It creates a spirit of anarchy, and wherever men commit the crime of lynching they are sowing the seeds of dissolution of society and of rottenness at heart of the community in which they live.

The natural impulse of every decent man is to do exactly as the mob does when it lynches aman; but the natural impulse is wrong. Men who give way to such a spirit of immediate revenge make murderers of themselves and plant in the hearts of their children and of the community the spirit of murder. The fearful record of homicides throughout the south is but the inevitable outgrowth of the unpunished mob which has lynched the law and lynched the sovereignty of the state.

Human life is held too cheaply in all parts of this country. The lynching spirit is not confined to the south, but wherever it breaks forth it is a crime against civilization, and there can be no regeneration of society until every member of every mob which lynches a man is punished to the extreme penalty of the law. If counties and states will not do this, then it will become absolutely incumbent upon the federal government to see than every where have the right of trial and of protection under the law until they are punished under the law. It matters not how deep may be the passions stirred by the vileness of the criminal, the lynching of the law cannot be excused on any ground whatver. There are excuses which can be given without number, but the excuses are not equal to the crime. No man can possibly consider the criminality which produces most of the lynching but by no means all of it, without feeling that he would be glad to take part in the lynching, but the yielding to that spirit is in itself a crime.

The Greeneville (S. C.) News emphasizes these facts with very great force in a recent editorial, in which it said:

"About a week ago, a negro was seized by a mob at Roxboro, N. C., and hurriedly lynched on the charge of attempted assault on a white woman. No opportunity was given him to clear himself of the charge. Now, it appears from the testimony of a white man, a contractor for whom the negro was working, that he was innocent of the charge. At the time the crime was committed, according to the contractor's published statement, the negro was at work on his job and didn't get off to go down until three hours later. If that is true, and it seems to be, the mob not only murdered a man but it murdered justice.

"The North Carolina press and public are seething with the story. The Charlotte Observer cries out that the honor of the state is at stake. There is more than that at stake. The honor of the state is besmirched and the majesty of the law trampled upon when even a guilty man is lynched. In this case justice, honor and law were lynched along with the man. The mob is a quadruple murderer.

'AUTHORITIES INVENTATION SHOWS LARGE EXODUS
Vicksburg, Miss., July 28th—Investigations carried on by local authorities indicate that more than 10,000 Negroes from this section of the state have left for various sections of the North in the last two months. The majority of them are determined to remain.

POLICE CHIEF FIRES
ON PASSING AUTOMOBILE
(Associated Negro Press)
Greenville, N. C., July 28th—Chief

Lester Jones, of the police department, lined into an automobile containing four Colored people, when the driver failed to stop after he called halt. He "supposed he car contained liquor." Two were injured.

LYNCHING IS DRIVING
LABOR AWAY
(Associated Negro press)
Memphis, Tenn., July 25th—Through trains passing via this city on the way to northern communities, for more than four months, have been crowded with men, women and children forming part of another Exodus to the North which is due to lynching and a general state of unrest among the people.

lawler-tobias-fort-scott-1920-08-11.A1:
MOBS HUNT FOR
FT. SCOTT NEGRO

Sheriffs of Two Counties Kept Busy Hiding Prisoner.

Victim of Murderer Was White World War Veteran.

LYNCHERS IN AUTOMOBILES

Other Negro Prisoners Moved From Threatened Jail.

Slayer Was Captured by Former Buddies of Victim.
Pittsburg, Kan., Aug. 12. — Learning that several motor cars loaded with members of a Fort Scott mob intent on a lynching had passed thru Arma, eight miles north of Pittsburg, Sheriff Charles Armour of Bourbon county hurried out of Pittsburg at 11 o'clock this morning with a negro who last night shot a white man at Fort Scott. The negro's name is unknown. He shot Howard Thomas, cement manufacturer, last night. It was said the negro came to Fort Scott three weeks ago.

Mob Gathered at Fort Scott.

A mob said to have numbered several thousand gathered at Fort Scott. Sheriff Armour got the negro away from Fort Scott and came to Pittsburg with him this morning. At 10:30 o'clock this morning a report from Arma stated that three motor cars loaded with men who displayed guns and ropes had passed thru there. It was said later that the pursuers had gone to Girard, the county seat of Crawford county, expecting to find that Sheriff Armour had put his prisoner in the county jail there. Sheriff Milt Gould of Crawford county, when he heard the report, immediately removed several negro prisoners from the jail.

Victim Was Service Man.

It was reported that several carloads of Fort Scott men had taken another route and gone thru Mulberry, altho their destination was not known.

At 11:30 o'clock it was reported from Fort Scott that Thomas had a good chance to recover. Thomas is a former service man and it was half a dozen former comrades who captured the negro early this morning at Garland, a town southeast of Fort Scott ten miles, after watching for him all night.

Wanted to Hang Negro.

Fort Scott, Kan., Aug. 12.—Between 100 and 200 automobiles filled with men left here early this morning in search of a negro, about 18 years old, name so far undetermined, who late yesterday shot five times Howard Thomas, secretary-treasurer of the Fort Scott Hydraulic Cement company.

The shooting followed an argument in Thomas's office over the negro's pay. It is thought that Thomas will recover. The expressed intention of members of the mob was to hang the negro if found. It was not known here where the negro was taken following his arrest early this morning by Sheriff Armour.

Taken to Jail at Joplin.

Joplin, Mo., Aug. 12.—Lawyer Tobias, the negro who shot Howard Thomas at Fort Scott last night, was brought to the Joplin jail shortly after noon today by the sheriff of Crawford county, Kansas, and the chief of police from Pittsburg. Bertillon measurements were taken of Tobias immediately upon arrival here, and Chief Myers said that he would be removed frm Joplin if there is any signs of a mob coming here.

A speedy automobile and a squad of officers armed with riot guns are on hand to take the negro away. Tobias says his home is in Mississippi and that he only recently moved to Fort Scott with his mother.

Tobias is charged with having shot and wounded Howard Thomas, a white man at Fort Scott. He was placed in the Joplin jail. URGE POLISH ENLISTMENT
Washington, Aug. 12.—It was understood that Prince Lubomirski had or would at a second conference, to be held with the secretary of state this afternoon, ask authorization of the United States to accept the numberless offers of enlistment in the Polish army which are being received daily from all parts of the country by the Polish legation.

POINTER DOG FOUND

A young black and white spotted pointer hunting dog has been found by the Humane society and can be had by application of the owner at the society offices on the third floor of the courthouse.
lawler-tobias-fort-scott-1920-08-11.A3:
BLEEDING KANSAS MOB
WOULD LYNCH A POOR
UNFORTUNATE BLACK
FOR SHOOTING A WHITE
Pittsburg, Kan., Aug. 12. — Learning that several motor cars loaded with members of a Fort Scott mob intent on a lynching, had passed through Arma, eight miles north of Pittsburg, Sheriff Clarence Armour of Bourbon county, hurried out of Pittsburg at 11 o'clock this morning, with a negro, who last night shot a white man at Fort Scott.

The negro, who is said to have come to Fort Scott about three weeks ago, shot Howard Thomas, a cement manufacturerer. Thomas was wounded in five places, but it is said he will recover.

A mob, said to have numbered thousands of persons, immediately began forming but Sheriff Armour eluded the gathering crowd and reached Pittsburg with the negro this morning.

Later it was reported that the pursuers had gone to Girard, the county seat of this (Crawford) county, expecting to find the sheriff and his prisoner in jail here. The prisoner was immediately removed with several other prisoners, from the jail. It was reported that several other motor cars loaded with Fort Scott men, had passed through Mulberry, but their destinations is as yet unknown.

The negro was employed by the cement company, of which Thomas is secretary and treasurer.
lawler-tobias-fort-scott-1920-08-11.A19:
This Sheriff Was No Wooley
(A. N. P. Service)
PITTSBURG, Kans., Sept. 3—Sheeriff Clarence Armour foiled a big Fort Scott mob bent on lynching a Negro who was charged with the killing of a white man at Fort Scott last Saturday night, by taking the man to Arma for safe keeping. The Negro says that he shot the man in self defense.

Club House at Pittsburg

(A. N. P. Services)
PITTSBURG, Pa., Sept. 3—Local colored men interested in athletics have opened their own club house at Chauncey Street and Wylie and Center Avenues, in the heart of the outer Hill District. A. M. Williams was the prime mover in the effort. The organization is known as the Central Amusement Company. Earl Johnson, the Negro distance runner, now in Antwerp with the American Olympic team is a member of the club.
